To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the p75 neurotrophin intracellular domain (ICD), a transcriptional factor, does not induce or enhance the activity of mitochondrial complex II, a key source of mitochondrial reactive oxygen production.

the p75 neurotrophin intracellular domain does not regulate the expression or activity of mitochondrial Complex II, and that the fenretinine-induced potentiation of neuroblastoma apoptosis by p75NTR does not result from transcriptional up-regulation of mitochondrial Complex II.
p75ICD and its active fragments do not affect expression or activity of mitochondrial Complex II.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which the neurotrophin p75 receptor potentiates fenretinide toxicity in neuroblastoma and the mechanism of fenretinide-mediated cell death.
the mechanism by which fenretinide potentiates apoptosis in neuroblastomas.
the mechanisms by which p75ICD potentiates the effects of fenretinide on neuroblastoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p75NTR and p75ICD are not involved in transcriptional regulation of mitochondrial Complex II.
the neurotrophin p75NTR does not regulate the expression of the subunits of Complex II.
the p75NTR-potentiated fenretinide-induced apoptosis of neuroblastoma cells does not involve transcriptional up-regulation of Complex II.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neuroprotective and pro-apoptotic effects of p75ICd are mediated by a transcriptional pathway that is distinct from the mitochondrial respiratory pathway.
the p75NTR-mediated enhancement of fenretinide-induced apoptosis is not due to transcriptional regulation of Complex II.
p75ICD does not affect the expression or activity of the Complex II.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fenretininde-potentiating activity of p75ICDs is not the result of transcriptionally mediated changes in expression of Complex II.
the fenretininide-potentiative effects of p75 are not due to the transcriptional enrichment of the mitochondria.
p75NTR does not regulate Complex II expression, and thus the mechanism by which p75NTR potentiates fenretinide-induced apoptosis remains unclear.
